Incoming packet is dropped silently by sk_filter()
allocated from pfmemalloc reserves and the corresponding socket is
not marked with the SOCK_MEMALLOC flag.
Igb driver allocates pages for DMA with __skb_alloc_page()
calls alloc_pages_node() with the __GFP_MEMALLOC flag. So
of OOM condition
column2: igb can get pages with pfmemalloc flag set.

column1: If an incoming packet hits the pfmemalloc page and is large enough
(small packets are copying into the memory
netdev_alloc_skb_ip_align()
dropped.
This behavior is ok under high memory pressure
that the igb driver reuses these mapped pages. So
dropping even if all memory issues are gone and there is a plenty
of free memory.
In my case
column2: some TCP sessions hang on a small percentage (< 0.1%)

column1: of machines days after OOMs.
Fix this by avoiding reuse of such pages.
